correctness.rationale: For finite E, independently uniform pre-draw edge U_t is independent of the predictable receptive indicator A_e(t). Conditional Borel–Cantelli, or stopping-time trials at successive receptive opportunities, gives infinitely many receptive selections whenever receptive opportunities occur infinitely often. Each selected receptive update forces c_e(t+1)>=gamma>0, incompatible with confidence convergence to zero, hence an edge tending to zero is eventually nonreceptive. The Li–Luo–Porter theorem supplies almost-sure confidence limits in {0,1} and equal limiting opinions for confidence-one edges; such edges are eventually receptive because confidence rises above 1/2 and opinion distance shrinks below 1/2. Taking the max of finitely many individual stabilization times proves the graph freezes almost surely. This respects strict threshold inequality and gamma=1, delta=0, mu=1/2 and disconnected graphs. Finite scripts do not prove infinite-time behavior; the published convergence premise is critical.
